newsitem.title: EGYPT: Jordan minister says Israel water row unresolved.
newsitem.headline: Jordan minister says Israel water row unresolved.

text.p: Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah said on Friday a secret summit meeting between Jordan's King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not resolve a dispute over water rights.

"The meeting ended without a deal on the main issue in question, which is the agreement in the Israeli-Jordanian peace treaty about water," Tarawnah told reporters shortly after arriving in Cairo for two-day talks with Egyptian officials.

"The meeting helped to bring our viewpoints closer but we still have to solve the technicalities of the issue and so we need to have more meetings." he added. "It is our right and we are very keen on implementing this part of the treaty."

The king and Netanyahu flew to the Jordanian Red Sea port of Aqaba on Thursday to talk about the stalled Middle East peace process and air their disagreements over water supplies Israel promised the parched Arab kingdom under their 1994 peace deal.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting with Netanyahu this week because of the water dispute, which Amman considers a breach of the peace deal.
But Israel's National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon, who is responsible for water, told Israel Radio both sides had "found solutions" that did not involve Israeli concessions.
Jordan is also growing frustrated with the deadlock in the peace process and Tarawnah told reporters he would confer with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to try to find ways to reactivate talks.
He said he would also deliver a message to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak from King Hussein.
Peace talks have been suspended since March when Netanyahu sent bulldozers to carve out a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Jordan and Egypt have said they fear a continued logjam in Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking would jeopardise regional stability.
